# Set up webhooks

CustomDomain™ sends a signed HTTPS request to your endpoint when a connection changes. Use it instead of polling.

Docs: https://docs.customdomain.ai/docs/webhooks/overview and https://docs.customdomain.ai/docs/webhooks/verifying-signatures

## Steps

### 1. Write the receiver first

The endpoint must be a public `https` address. `localhost` and private addresses are refused at registration, so use a tunnel or a deployed preview while developing. See "The receiver" below.

### 2. Register the endpoint from your server

Use an API key, from an environment variable, never in the browser:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.customdomain.ai/v1/webhooks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CUSTOMDOMAIN_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"url":"https://your-app.example/webhooks/customdomain","events":["connection.live","connection.failed"]}'
```

- The answer holds `id` and a `secret` that starts `whsec_`. The secret is shown once. The person stores it in their secret store as `CUSTOMDOMAIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Do not print it in chat or commit it.
- An empty `events` list, or `"*"`, subscribes to every event. Subscribe only to events that exist; the catalog is on the overview page.
- A widget token with the default `connect` scope cannot register an endpoint. Use the API key.
- `GET /v1/webhooks` lists endpoints without secrets. `DELETE /v1/webhooks/{id}` removes one.
- A Sandbox (test mode) application has its own endpoints, made with its own key. Register one there to test, and register again on the live application at go live.

### 3. Verify every delivery

Each request carries three headers:

- `X-JE-Timestamp`: unix seconds when it was signed.
- `X-JE-Signature`: `sha256=` and a hex HMAC-SHA256 of the string `<timestamp>.<raw body>`, keyed by the endpoint's secret.
- `X-JE-Event-Id`: the event id, the same on every retry.

Rules:

- Sign the exact bytes received. Read the raw body before any JSON parsing. Do not re-serialize.
- Compare in constant time.
- Reject a timestamp older than your window. Five minutes is the recommended window.
- Answer a bad signature with `401` and do nothing else.

### 4. Answer fast, then work

- Return any `2xx` within 15 seconds. Do slow work after you answer, from a queue or job.
- Network errors, `5xx` and `429` are retried with growing delays, up to 12 attempts. Any other `4xx` is treated as a permanent failure and is not retried. So return `5xx` for a temporary problem on your side, and never return `4xx` for one.
- The same event can arrive more than once. Deduplicate on `X-JE-Event-Id` (the `id` in the body). Make the handler safe to run twice.

### 5. Test

- Send a test delivery to one endpoint with `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}:test`. It sends a `webhook.test` event to that endpoint only.
- Connect a `.test` name in the Sandbox. Its events are signed and delivered like real ones and carry `"sandbox": true`.
- `GET /v1/webhook-deliveries` shows recent outcomes (`attempts`, `status_code`, `delivered`, `error`).

## The receiver

Node, using the built in crypto module. This one keeps the body as text so the signature matches.

```js
import crypto from "node:crypto";

export function verify(rawBody, timestamp, signature, secret, toleranceSeconds = 300) {
  const ts = Number.parseInt(timestamp, 10);
  if (!Number.isFinite(ts)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - ts) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected =
    "sha256=" + crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${ts}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  const a = Buffer.from(signature || "");
  const b = Buffer.from(expected);
  return a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
}
```

Next.js route handler (`app/webhooks/customdomain/route.ts`):

```ts
import { verify } from "@/lib/customdomain-verify";

export async function POST(req: Request) {
  const raw = await req.text(); // the exact bytes, before any parsing
  const ok = verify(
    raw,
    req.headers.get("x-je-timestamp") ?? "",
    req.headers.get("x-je-signature") ?? "",
    process.env.CUSTOMDOMAIN_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
  );
  if (!ok) return new Response("bad signature", { status: 401 });

  const event = JSON.parse(raw);
  if (event.sandbox) return new Response("ok"); // skip test mode events where they would touch real data
  // Deduplicate on event.id, then act on event.type.
  return new Response("ok");
}
```

Express: use `express.raw({ type: "application/json" })` on this route only, so the body stays as bytes, and pass `req.body` to `verify`.

## What an event looks like

A flat JSON object: `id`, `type`, `user_id`, `domain`, `provider`, `propagation_status`, `data`, `created_at`, and fields that apply to the event (such as `connection_id`, `error_code` and `error_message` on a failure). Fields that do not apply are left out.

- `user_id` is the `end_user_ref` you passed when the customer connected. Use it to find the customer in your own data. It is missing when none was passed. A value that starts `console:` comes from the console's own tests, not a customer, so skip it.
- `sandbox: true` marks a test mode event. A live event has no such field.

## Events most products use

| Event | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| `connection.live` | Mark the customer's domain as connected. |
| `connection.failed` | Tell the customer the records never appeared, and link them to help. |
| `connection.disconnected` | Mark the domain removed. |
| `certificate.failed`, `certificate.expiring` | Warn about a certificate problem. |
| `domain.record_missing`, `domain.record_restored` | React to DNS drift, where drift alerts are switched on. |

The full list and each payload: https://docs.customdomain.ai/docs/webhooks/overview#event-catalog

## Rules

- Never log the secret, the signature header together with the secret, or full request bodies that hold customer data.
- Do not act on an event before the signature check passes.
- Store the secret as an environment variable name in code; the value lives only in the secret store.
